title: NCLT Kolkata: Homebuyers' 10% Insolvency Threshold Is Measured on Actual Bookings, Not Developer's Claimed Allottee Count
case_name: Evanie Eco Nest Home Buyers Association v. Evanie Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.
card_summary: Fifty-nine homebuyers claiming a default of about Rs 3.43 crore filed a Section 7 petition, and their developer said the project had 966 allottees so the applicants fell short of the 10% threshold for homebuyers under the IBC. The Bench held the threshold is worked out on actual bookings on the filing date, not proposed units, and found the developer had not proved its own count. The petition was admitted.
card_tip: A developer resisting a homebuyers' insolvency petition must prove its allottee numbers with evidence; an unsubstantiated higher count, or one based on unsold or proposed units, will not defeat the 10% threshold.
verification_notes: Order date (9 October 2026), bench composition and default figure (Rs 3,43,39,345) confirmed across Taxscan, TaxGuru and Legal Era reports; no formal case/CP number was given in the reports consulted.
